Maya (AE): FYI customer AcmeHealth wants a 2-week air-gapped POC next month. They asked about packaging, upgrade cadence (only quarterly windows), signing, and a ballpark for a 3-node pilot. Any immediate blockers?
Jonah (SE): Do we know target infra? k8s vs VMs? distro/kernel/container runtime? That affects bundle format (tar vs OVA vs operator).
Maya (AE): They're running RHEL VMs with containerd but might want k8s later. I'll confirm exact versions. Legal already flagged HSM/FIPS requirements.
Priya (Solutions Eng): For airgap we support operator-based and standalone bootstrap. Key pieces: signed minibundles (chunked), side-load via USB/sneakernet, or HTTP shuttle if allowed. Prereqs we typically ask for: containerd >=1.5/1.6, glibc >=2.28, and kernel >=4.18. If baremetal, use bootstrap image.
Sahil (Security): Security Qs to answer: SBOM availability, code signing key provenance, HSM/KMS integration, FIPS cert level, vulnerability disclosure cadence. Also confirm whether they require attestation from our HSM or will accept customer-provided HSM.
Jonah (SE): Note on upgrades: we can do rolling canary upgrades via operator when network allows. In sealed sites where no egress, upgrades are manual: produce signed delta bundles for the exact deployed commit. That aligns with quarterly windows but means ops must stage two windows during the POC (canary then full).
Maya (AE): They explicitly want quarterly cadences only. Legal: needs SBOM + evidence of signing provenance. Customer asked how big minibundles are for quantized vs FP16 models.
Priya (Solutions Eng): Quantized artifacts are smaller but model shard layout matters. Minibundle (runtime + model shards) typically 4-12GB depending on model. We can provide a trimmed dist (8-bit) for the POC to keep media <=16GB if they want USB.
Jonah (SE): Delta update flow (high level): we generate manifest -> chunk diffs -> sign each chunk -> customer verifies signature and applies. Example install command we give ops teams:
```
# sample airgap bootstrap
redwoodctl bootstrap --bundle /mnt/usb/minibundle.tar.gz --license /mnt/usb/license.key --install-mode airgap
```
Priya (Solutions Eng): Also will need offline CA cert + allowed fingerprint list so our operator trusts the local certs. If they want telemetry disabled, we'll need to ship with telemetry opt-out and a local metrics sink (Prometheus pushgateway or file).
Maya (AE): Pricing question: what do we usually quote for 2-week pilot + HSM work? Customer asked for a ballpark to include in internal budget.
Jonah (SE): We normally cover 2-week evals under trial credits. HSM integration + custom minibundle packaging is billable: estimate 3-5 ENG days (SE + EngOps) for first integration + per-bundle Ops time (0.5-1 day) for each signed minibundle. For longer reserved pilots we switch to a provisional monthly license. I'll draft a short SOW bullet list.
Sahil (Security): Blocker: export control / model license. If we're shipping third-party weights, legal/export may need extra review for a healthcare customer. Need to confirm model provenance and any restricted components.
Maya (AE): Action items: @Priya to produce minibundle checklist + size estimates; @Jonah to author upgrade runbook with manual side-load steps and two-window plan; @Sahil to prepare security Q answers (SBOM, signing, HSM), and I'll get customer infra versions. I'll loop in AcmeHealth infra lead.
ops-bot: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/airgap-poc|airgap-runbook> (contains bundle checklist, signing guide, sample manifests)
Priya (Solutions Eng): I'll have a draft minibundle checklist and sample bundle by EOD tomorrow. Need customer's infra contact and containerd/kernel versions.
Maya (AE): Customer contact: susan.c@acmehealth.com. Target start week Apr 12.
Jonah (SE): For the runbook I'll include: preflight (kernel/containerd/glibc), signing verification commands, delta apply steps, and rollback notes. Example verify snippet: `sha256sum -c minibundle.sha256 && redwoodctl apply --bundle minibundle.tar.gz --verify-signature`
Sahil (Security): I'll prep SBOM export (CycloneDX), signing key lineage, and an HSM integration checklist. If they require FIPS attestation we'll need to pull certs from infra.
Maya (AE): Great. If no one objects I'll send the customer a one-pager with these constraints and ask for the infra versions and their maintenance windows. :thumbsup:
